title: Donation swap (sUSDS -> waUSDC) is executed with limitRaw=0 and only the post-unwrap USDC is slippage-checked, enabling sandwich extraction inside the same unlock callback
description:
Inside unlockCallback the donation phase performs IBalancerVault.swap(VaultSwapParams({ ..., amountGivenRaw: donationSUSDS, limitRaw: 0, ... })) — i.e., it accepts any non-zero amount of waUSDC out. The slippage gate is moved to a single require(usdcReceived >= minUSDC) after IERC4626(waUsdc).redeem(...). This conflates two independent slippage surfaces into one:

1. Spot price of sUSDS/waUSDC on the Balancer V3 pool at execution time (sandwichable). This determines waUsdcReceived.
2. waUSDC <> USDC redemption rate on the Aave wrapper. This determines usdcReceived from waUsdcReceived.

Because limitRaw is zero, the pooler effectively can only protect against a combined drop. If the swap leg is sandwiched while the waUSDC->USDC rate stays put (which it does — Aave waUSDC's ERC4626 rate updates only as Aave interest accrues and is therefore effectively constant within a block), then any sandwich on the swap leg directly reduces the USDC eventually delivered to batchMinter by the price-impact percentage of the front-run/back-run.

Worse, the swap and the addLiquidity execute in the SAME unlock callback. An attacker can move the sUSDS/waUSDC pool ahead of the swap, then the sUSDS/phUSD pool ahead of the addLiquidity, with a single bundled transaction.

Re-validation note (yield-claim-nft-07, HEAD 1bb956c): Donation block at lines 217-249 is byte-identical to c67d3c9. Finding carries forward unchanged; locations adjusted (was 214-243, now 217-249 due to the import addition shifting bodies forward by 3 lines).
exploit_path:
Setup: BalancerPoolerV2 holds X sUSDS. batchDonationSize = 50 means donationSUSDS = X/2 will flow through the swap.

Attack:
1. MEV bot observes pool(minBPT, minUSDC) in the mempool.
2. Bundle:
   a. Frontrun: flashloan sUSDS, swap sUSDS -> waUSDC on the sUSDS/waUSDC pool, pushing waUSDC's price down.
   b. pool() executes. The donation swap goes through at the worse price. Because limitRaw=0, even an aggressive sandwich does not trigger a revert here.
   c. Unwrap waUSDC -> USDC.
   d. Backrun: swap waUSDC -> sUSDS on the same pool, repaying the flashloan and pocketing the spread.

Profit estimate: For a donationSUSDS of $50k against a $3M-deep sUSDS/waUSDC pool with 0.04% fee, a 100bps sandwich extracts roughly $300-$500 per pool() call after gas. Repeated weekly: ~$15k-$25k/year leaked to MEV.
mainnet_realism: Balancer V3 sUSDS/waUSDC Aave-Boosted pools exist on mainnet. Pool depth varies; smaller boosted pools (<$5M TVL) regularly carry >50bps slippage on $50k trades. waUSDC (Aave wrapped USDC) is a standard ERC4626 with negligible deviation from its share price during a single block.
recommendation: Replace limitRaw: 0 with a caller-supplied per-leg slippage cap, e.g., add a minWaUsdc parameter to pool(). Also enforce that the donation swap and addLiquidity occur in separate transactions. Add a deadline parameter to pool().
severity_rationale: Carry-forward from report-6 (Medium). Hard-coded limitRaw: 0 on the donation swap conflates two slippage surfaces into one. The function is callable only via onlyAuthorizedPooler — value leak with stated external requirements (public mempool submission + loose operator-set minUSDC). Medium per C4.
poc_notes: PoC from report-6 still applies — donation block (lines 217-249 at HEAD) is byte-identical to c67d3c9. Original PoC: at 500 sUSDS attack size, USDC delivered to batchMinter drops from 219.0 USDC -> 139.1 USDC (36.51% loss); attacker recovers 570.99 sUSDS for 500 sUSDS input.
